:::{#exm-difference-quotient}
#### The difference quotient of $x^2$ at $1$

For $f(x) = x^2$, $c = 1$, and $h \ne 0$,

$$
\ba
\frac{f(1 + h) - f(1)}{h}
&= \frac{(1 + h)^2 - 1}{h}
&& \text{(substitute into } f \text{)}
\\
&= \frac{1 + 2h + h^2 - 1}{h}
&& \text{(expand } (1 + h)^2 \text{)}
\\
&= \frac{2h + h^2}{h}
&& \text{(} 1 - 1 = 0 \text{)}
\\
&= 2 + h,
&& \text{(divide by } h \ne 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

which tends to $2$ as $h \to 0$ (@def-limit).
With $h = 0.1$ the difference quotient is $2 + 0.1 = 2.1$:
the line through $(1, 1)$ and $(1.1, 1.21)$ has slope $\tfrac{1.21 - 1}{0.1} = \tfrac{0.21}{0.1} = 2.1$.

:::
